topic: Status marks for durational in with activities
claim: Non-bounding duration adjuncts “cannot appear with clauses denoting imperfective situations (activities and states)”, marked as anomalous: #I wrote letters in an hour. Under the heading “Shortness implicature” the same page says “it is infelicitous to modify with at least” and marks it ungrammatical: The doctor will arrive in at most an hour / ∗at least an hour.
evidence_summary: Page 668 stars the same clash of in with an activity: She ran for ten minutes / ∗in ten minutes. So does Ch. 3 p. 122 [18ic], He played tennis for an hour / ∗in an hour, labelled “[activity]”. Ch. 3 p. 122 also ties implicature to cancellation: “We have spoken here of an implicature because of the possibility of cancellation”. The notational conventions (p. xii) use ∗ for ungrammatical and # for semantically or pragmatically anomalous.
finding: The same aspectual clash is marked # here but ∗ on p. 668 and in Ch. 3, and the ∗ on at least marks an effect the prose attributes to an implicature. Clashes between aspect and adjunct lie near the border of grammar and meaning, which partly excuses the variation, but the book doesn’t say which status it intends.
inference: Is durational in with an activity ungrammatical or anomalous?

evidence.passage: §7.4, p. 709. “cannot appear with clauses denoting imperfective situations (activities and states)”
evidence.example: Page 668, She ran for ten minutes / ∗in ten minutes; Ch. 3 p. 122 [18ic].
evidence.establishes: The same clash carries different status marks.
